stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: A cache of bronze fishhooks, net weights, and carved bone needles recovered from a flooded settlement in southern Finland ______ archaeologists a rare look at how Iron Age communities fished inland lakes. Because the objects lay sealed beneath waterlogged clay for centuries, even the fine barbs on the hooks remain intact.
explanation: Cross out the prepositional phrases "of bronze fishhooks, net weights, and carved bone needles" and "from a flooded settlement in southern Finland," along with the modifier "recovered." What's left is "A cache ______ archaeologists a rare look." "Cache" is singular, so you need the singular verb "gives." The present tense also matches "remain" in the next sentence.

A.why: You made the verb agree with the plural list "fishhooks, net weights, and carved bone needles" instead of the true subject, "cache," which is singular.

C.why: "Are giving" is plural. You probably matched it to the plural nouns inside the "of" phrase, but the subject is the singular "cache."

D.why: "Have given" is a plural form. The singular subject "cache" would need "has given," so this choice fails on number.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Soil scientist Marisol Okafor has spent a decade studying cover crops, plants grown between cash-crop seasons to protect the soil. Her most recent trial, which compared rye, clover, and radish plantings across forty Iowa fields, ______ that rye can reduce nitrogen runoff by nearly a third.
explanation: Cross out the "which" clause between the commas and you're left with "Her most recent trial ______ that rye can reduce nitrogen runoff." "Trial" is singular, so the verb must be singular: "has shown."

A.why: You matched the verb to the plural nouns just before the blank ("plantings," "fields") rather than to the singular subject, "trial."

B.why: "Show" is the plural present form. It sounds right after "forty Iowa fields," but "fields" sits inside the "which" clause and isn't the subject.

C.why: "Were showing" is plural, so it can't go with the singular subject "trial." You were probably pulled in by the plural nouns in the interrupting clause.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Each winter, monarch butterflies from across eastern North America gather in the fir forests of central Mexico. The number of butterflies arriving at these mountain sites ______ sharply since the 1990s, a trend researchers link to the loss of milkweed, the only plant on which monarch caterpillars feed.
explanation: Cross out "of butterflies arriving at these mountain sites" and the sentence reads "The number ______ sharply since the 1990s." "Number" is singular, and the time marker "since the 1990s" calls for present perfect, so "has declined" is correct.

B.why: You matched the verb to "butterflies" or "sites," but both sit inside the prepositional phrase. The subject is the singular "number."

C.why: "Are declining" is plural and doesn't agree with the singular subject "number." The plural nouns in the "of" phrase are decoys.

D.why: "Were declining" is plural, so it doesn't agree with "number." It also doesn't fit the "since the 1990s" time marker.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: The Voices Archive Project, an effort that has recorded hundreds of speakers of Ainu, Yuchi, and other threatened languages, ______ its entire audio collection freely available online. As a result, linguists and community members anywhere can listen to storytelling, songs, and everyday conversation in languages that may soon have no fluent speakers.
explanation: Cross out the appositive between the commas ("an effort that has recorded... threatened languages") and you're left with "The Voices Archive Project ______ its entire audio collection freely available." A named project is one singular thing, so the verb is "makes."

A.why: You matched the verb to "languages," the plural noun just before the blank. That noun is inside the appositive, and the subject is the singular "Project."

B.why: "Are making" is plural. A named organization like "The Voices Archive Project" may sound like many people, but grammatically it is singular.

D.why: "Have made" is plural and doesn't agree with the singular subject "Project." The plural list inside the appositive is the trap.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Telescopes that detect infrared light can reveal objects far older than anything visible to the naked eye. One of the faint galaxies catalogued in a recent deep-field survey ______ visible only because of light that began its journey about 13 billion years ago, when the universe was still young. Studying such objects helps astronomers understand how early galaxies formed.
explanation: The subject is "One," and "of the faint galaxies catalogued in a recent deep-field survey" is a prepositional phrase you can cross out. "One" is singular, so you need "is." The present tense also matches "helps" in the next sentence.

A.why: You made the verb agree with "galaxies," but "one of" makes the subject singular. "Galaxies" is only the object of "of."

B.why: "Have been" is plural and doesn't agree with the singular subject "One." The plural noun "galaxies" is the decoy.

C.why: "Were" is plural (the singular past would be "was"), so it doesn't agree with "One." You probably matched it to "galaxies."

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Folklorist Anaïs Duret spent much of the 1970s recording stories told in the fishing villages of Brittany, France. Every one of the tales in her published collection ______ some version of the same motif: a sailor who ignores a warning from the sea and never returns home. Duret argued that the motif reflected the real dangers of the region's coastline.
explanation: Cross out "of the tales in her published collection" and you're left with "Every one ______ some version of the same motif." "Every one" is singular, so the singular "contains" is correct.

B.why: You matched the verb to "tales" or "collection" instead of the true subject. "Every one" is always singular, so "contain" doesn't agree.

C.why: "Have contained" is plural. The plural noun "tales" sits inside the prepositional phrase and isn't the subject, so it can't set the verb's number.

D.why: "Were containing" is plural and doesn't agree with the singular "Every one." You were probably misled by the plural "tales."

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Nineteenth-century surveyor Tomasz Wierzbicki drew detailed maps of the river valleys of eastern Galicia. His careful rendering of elevations, riverbanks, and village boundaries ______ why historians still consult the maps today, even though far more precise satellite surveys now exist.
explanation: Cross out "of elevations, riverbanks, and village boundaries" and the sentence reads "His careful rendering ______ why historians still consult the maps." The subject is "rendering," which is singular, so you need "explains."

A.why: You made the verb agree with the plural list right before the blank. That list belongs to the "of" phrase, and the subject is the singular "rendering."

C.why: "Have explained" is plural. The main noun of the subject phrase is "rendering," which is singular, so it would need "has explained."

D.why: "Are explaining" is plural and doesn't agree with "rendering." The plural nouns "riverbanks" and "boundaries" are the decoys.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: The sea otters that live along the rocky coast of central California ______ a key role in protecting the region's kelp forests. By eating sea urchins, which graze on kelp, the otters keep urchin populations from stripping the seafloor bare and allow the towering underwater forests to regrow.
explanation: Cross out the "that" clause ("that live along the rocky coast of central California") and you're left with "The sea otters ______ a key role." "Otters" is plural, so you need the plural verb "play." The present tense matches "keep" and "allow" in the next sentence.

A.why: You made the verb agree with "California," the singular noun right before the blank. That noun is inside the relative clause, and the subject is the plural "otters."

B.why: "Has played" is singular. It sounds natural after "coast" or "California," but neither is the subject. "Otters" is plural.

D.why: "Is playing" is singular and doesn't agree with the plural subject "otters." The singular nouns in the "that" clause are the trap.
